en: 'Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di and Ahmad ibn Janab both narrated to us from 'Isa—and the wording is Ibn Hujr's—'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from his brother 'Abdullah ibn 'Urwah, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: Eleven women sat together, and covenanted and pledged that they would not conceal anything of the news of their husbands. The first one said: "My husband is lean camel meat on the top of a rugged mountain; it is not smooth so that one could climb it, nor is it fat so that one would take it away." The second one said: "As for my husband, I will not broadcast his news, for I fear I could not leave it unfinished; if I mention him, I will mention his protruding veins and belly humps." The third one said: "My husband is very tall; if I speak, I am divorced, and if I remain silent, I am left in suspense." The fourth one said: "My husband is like the night of Tihamah: neither hot nor cold, with neither fear nor weariness." The fifth one said: "My husband, when he enters, is like a leopard, and when he goes out, is like a lion, and he does not ask about what he left behind." The sixth one said: "My husband, if he eats, he consumes all, and if he drinks, he drains it to the last drop, and if he lies down, he wraps himself up, and he does not insert his hand to find out my sorrow." The seventh one said: "My husband is heavy-headed and dim-witted; every ailment that exists is in him; he fractures your head, or breaks your bones, or combines both against you." The eighth one said: "My husband: the scent is the scent of sweet zarnab, and the touch is the touch of a hare." The ninth one said: "My husband is of lofty tent-pole, long sword-belt, abundant ashes, and his house is close to the meeting place." The tenth one said: "My husband is Malik, and what a man is Malik! Malik is better than all of that. He possesses camels having many resting-places and few pastures; whenever they hear the sound of the lute, they know with certainty that they are doomed to slaughter." The eleventh one said: "My husband is Abu Zar', and what a man is Abu Zar'! He adorned my ears with ornaments until they swung, filled my upper arms with fat, and delighted me so that I became pleased with myself. He found me among people of a few sheep in hardship, and brought me among people of horses whinnying, camels groaning, grain-threshers, and winnowers. In his presence, I speak and am not disparaged; I sleep and slumber until morning; and I drink until my thirst is fully quenched. And the mother of Abu Zar'—what a woman is the mother of Abu Zar'! Her grain-bags are huge and bulky, and her house is spacious. And the son of Abu Zar'—what a boy is the son of Abu Zar'! His sleeping place is like a stripped palm branch, and the arm of a four-month-old goat satisfies him. And the daughter of Abu Zar'—what a girl is the daughter of Abu Zar'! Obedient to her father and obedient to her mother, filling out her cloak, and the grief of her neighbor. And the slave-girl of Abu Zar'—what a maid is the slave-girl of Abu Zar'! She does not broadcast our talk abroad, does not squander our provisions, and does not fill our house with rubbish like a bird's nest. She said: Abu Zar' went out while the milk-skins were being churned, and he met a woman with whom were two sons of hers like two leopards, playing from beneath her waist with two pomegranates. So he divorced me and married her. After him, I married a noble man: he rode a spirited thoroughbred horse, carried a Khatti spear, brought home abundant grazing livestock to me in the evening, and gave me a pair from every kind of livestock. He said: 'Eat, O Umm Zar', and provide for your family.' Yet if I were to gather everything he gave me, it would not reach the smallest vessel of Abu Zar'!" 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to me: "I was to you like Abu Zar' was to Umm Zar'."
